newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists criticise EU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists criticise EU stability pact.

text.p: France's opposition Socialist Party said on Monday that a stability pact struck by European Union leaders was a "bad deal" that went too far in meeting Germany's demand for strict enforcement of budget discipline.
"We don't understand Finance Minister Jean Arthuis' euphoric reaction because it was a bad deal," Socialist Party spokesman Francois Hollande told a weekly news conference.

"It's a bad deal in the sense that the stability pact has incorporated the most rigorous viewpoint, notably that of the Germans, to add a measure to the Maastricht Treaty that had not been envisaged," he said.

"In so far as Maastricht had set convergence criteria, it did not include sanctions. There, we went beyond Maastricht," Hollande said. "And yet we're extremely vague on the political authority that is expected to act as a counterweight to the European central bank."

The stability pact agreement, struck at an EU summit in Dublin over the weekend, has been welcomed by the financial markets. The foreign exchange markets have broadly interpreted it as weakening sentiment on the mark.
